title: Feedback Zeitgeist — compact synthesis and engineering asks (May 2026)
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable roll-up of the last 3 weeks of inbound customer signals (support tickets, CSM calls, pilot notes). Goal is to surface small, fast engineering patches and a couple of focused spikes that materially reduce customer friction for the highest-traffic scenarios.

Summary (topline):
- Recurring themes: unexpected token-cost spikes for long chat sessions, KV-cache fragmentation causing memory churn on Dedicated pools, embeddings drift vs. stored vectors (semantic mismatch after model updates), and a handful of feature asks around per-route timeout controls and deterministic fallback routing.
- Customers impacted: 8 mid-market and 3 enterprise pilots reported pain that matches the top themes (weighted toward multi-turn chat + retrieval workloads).
- Quick wins (low-effort): 4 items we can ship as small patches or config defaults.
- Spikes (investigate): 2 focused engineering spikes to clarify cost vs. quality tradeoffs for quant profiles and a lightweight local eval harness for embedding drift.

Field vignettes (real customer quotes / context):
1) LegalTech pilot (Enterprise): "Token bills doubled after a 72-hour conversation thread — we didn't change prompts." Tech notes: long multi-turn threads (avg 6k tokens/user) + few prefix-cached messages triggered unoptimized batching. Ticket: JIRA-CS-4432.
2) Marketplace platform (Mid-market): "Embeddings start returning unrelated results after model patch." Observed: nightly model refresh with subtle parameter change, stored vectors unchanged, semantic recall dropped 12% on retrieval eval. Ticket: JIRA-CS-4499.
3) Finance analytics (Dedicated): "GPU OOMs intermittently on dedicated pool, SRE had to reboot nodes." Logs show kv-cache fragmentation + bursty requests with high seq lengths. Slack thread: #platform-incidents ts:1649991234.

Prioritized quick fixes (ranked by impact * confidence):
A) Default per-route soft timeout (30s) + visible fallback counter in Console (owner: Amara). Why: prevents runaway requests and gives customers an explicit signal to route to cheaper model. Estimated effort: 2 engineer-days + 1 UX day. Risk: low. Linked artifact: JIRA-ENG-9876.
B) Enable conservative KV-cache compaction on Dedicated pools (config flag + rolling restart) — short-term mitigation for fragmentation. Owner: SRE/Infra. Estimated effort: 3 engineer-days (ops-heavy). Risk: medium (requires rolling strategy).
C) Prompt-size billing diagnostic flag (opt-in) that annotates invoices with top n contributing requests and token distributions. Owner: Finance + Backend. Effort: 4 engineer-days + small schema change. Risk: low.
D) Embedding stability advisory + automated nightly sanity check (lightweight eval) that emails CSM on >10% drift. Owner: CS + Applied ML. Effort: 3 engineer-days for probe + 1 day CSM workflow. Risk: low-medium.

Proposed spikes (timebox 2 weeks each):
1) Quantization quality vs cost spike (owner: Applied ML + Serving Runtime). Objective: measure quality delta for top 10 customer prompts across quant profiles we plan to recommend. Deliverable: a matrix with quality scores (ROUGE/semantic-sim) and token-level cost estimates, plus a recommendation heuristic for Optimize. Why: several customers reported hallucination/regression concerns after we suggested aggressive quantization. Impact: medium-high.
2) Embedding-drift local harness (owner: Applied ML + CS). Objective: build a reproducible, fast harness that (a) computes nightly recall on a small seeded dataset per-customer, (b) reports both semantic distance shift and a short list of top changed nearest neighbors. Deliverable: a runnable script + docs + alert config. Impact: high for retrieval-heavy customers.

Open questions / unknowns to surface in next sync:
- How many customers would opt into the billing diagnostic flag? (CS to poll top 20 pilots by 2026-05-21).
- Is KV-cache compaction compatible with multi-tenant pods on Dedicated without violating data isolation SLAs? (SRE to validate).
- For embedding drift: do we throttle nightly checks to keep costs negligible for large customers? Proposal: sample 1k queries/day.

Risk and mitigation notes:
- Any change to default quantization or batching should be accompanied by a small rollback path and regression gating in the rollout console.
- Rolling KV-cache compaction requires a canary on one pool with low traffic; create a canary runbook.

Quick implementation roadmap (next 6 weeks):
Week 1 (this week): finalize owner assignments, create JIRA cards (Amara + Priya).
Week 2: ship per-route soft timeout UI + backend flag. Small CSM communication template drafted.
Week 3: SRE implements KV-cache compaction flag and runbook; run one canary on a low-traffic Dedicated pool.
Week 4-5: run quantization spike; run embedding harness prototype against 3 pilot datasets.
Week 6: compile results, propose specific Optimize recommendations and a short CS playbook for embedding alerts.

Action items (named owners):
- Amara: open UI ticket + one-pager on soft timeouts (due 2026-05-14).
- SRE (Diego): feasibility of KV compaction w/ data isolation note + canary plan (due 2026-05-17).
- Applied ML (Liam): scope quantization spike + dataset pull list (due 2026-05-16).
- Priya: poll top 20 pilots about billing diagnostic opt-in and assemble sample invoice extract (due 2026-05-21).
- CS: prepare 2-sentence customer advisory about embedding drift and a recommended short-term mitigation (due 2026-05-15).

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep spike artifacts minimal and reproducible — we want clear pass/fail signals.
- Track all customer notification drafts in CONFLUENCE-12345 so legal can review.
- If quantization spike shows >5% quality regression for any pilot, recommend conservative default and attach a toggle in Optimize.

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot):
- Pilot set: 11 active pilots; 3 enterprise, 8 mid-market.
- Reported token-bill anomalies: 8 incidents across 5 customers in last 30 days.
- Embedding recall drop: avg 12% on 3 flagged customers after model refresh.
- OOM incidents: 2 in last 14 days tied to Dedicated pools.

End notes: this is intentionally compact — for the next sync (2026-05-20) we should have JIRA cards for the quick fixes and spike charters. Keep this doc as the single-page conversation starter; heavier write-ups live in linked Confluence and JIRA cards.

Unresolved phrasing / scratch: consider naming the KV-compaction plan "gentle-squeeze" and log the name in runbook.

-- Priya (notes captured from CS standups, SRE triage, and two pilot calls)
